name: SQL Injection
description: Untrusted input can alter the structure of a database query when it is concatenated into SQL.
impact: May expose, change, or delete database data depending on application privileges.
remediation: Use parameterized queries or a safe ORM API. Validate inputs and use least-privilege database accounts.

name: Cross-Site Scripting
description: Untrusted data reaches an HTML or script-sensitive output context without appropriate encoding or sanitization.
impact: May allow attacker-controlled browser content in another user's session, depending on the sink and context.
remediation: Prefer safe text rendering and context-aware output encoding. Sanitize HTML only when HTML is actually required.

name: Hardcoded Credentials
description: Secrets embedded in source code can be exposed through repositories, logs, builds, or source distribution.
impact: Could enable unauthorized use of the associated service or account if the credential remains valid.
remediation: Use environment variables or a secret manager and rotate exposed credentials.

name: Path Traversal
description: User-controlled path components can escape an intended directory if paths are not constrained.
impact: May expose or modify files outside the intended application directory.
remediation: Canonicalize paths, enforce an allowlist, use a fixed base directory, and reject unsafe path components.

name: OS Command Injection
description: Untrusted data reaches a shell or operating-system command execution sink.
impact: May cause unintended operating-system operations under the application's privileges.
remediation: Avoid shell execution, use argument arrays, strict allowlists, and never pass untrusted strings to a shell.

name: Code Injection
description: Application data can be interpreted as executable code through dynamic evaluation APIs.
impact: May allow execution of unintended application code if attacker-controlled data reaches the evaluator.
remediation: Remove dynamic evaluation and use structured parsing or explicit dispatch.

name: Server-Side Request Forgery
description: A server makes outbound requests using a destination influenced by an untrusted user.
impact: May expose internal services or cause unintended requests from the application's network context.
remediation: Use destination allowlists, URL validation, and network-level restrictions where appropriate.

name: Weak Cryptography
description: Obsolete or inappropriate cryptographic primitives can weaken confidentiality or integrity.
impact: Security-sensitive data may be easier to compromise depending on the use case.
remediation: Use modern cryptographic algorithms and dedicated password hashing such as Argon2id, scrypt, or bcrypt for passwords.

name: Debug Mode
description: Production debug features can disclose internal implementation details.
impact: Stack traces or debug interfaces may reveal sensitive implementation information.
remediation: Disable debug mode in production and use controlled error responses.

name: Permissive CORS
description: Overly broad cross-origin policies can expose browser-accessible resources to untrusted origins.
impact: Depending on credentials and endpoints, untrusted web origins may gain browser access to resources.
remediation: Allow only trusted origins and use the narrowest CORS policy required.

name: Authentication Weakness
description: Weak authentication or session handling can allow unauthorized account access.
impact: Could result in account takeover or unauthorized access when combined with a concrete authentication flaw.
remediation: Use secure session handling, strong authentication, safe cookie attributes, and appropriate authorization checks.

name: Security Misconfiguration
description: Missing security controls or unsafe defaults can increase attack surface.
impact: May expose application functionality or data unnecessarily.
remediation: Apply secure defaults, minimize exposed functionality, and configure appropriate security headers and access controls.
